Subject: Simulated throughput & token levers — MAP assumptions for Novena pilot

Hi Arman / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I attached a first-pass MAP focused on the token and throughput assumptions you asked us to validate before legal/proc starts (MAP_Novena_v0.3.pdf). High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm expected peak concurrent sessions for triage flows (you mentioned 50–80 CCU during business hours).
- Confirm average prompt/response lengths (tokens) for clinical triage vs. scheduling flows.
- Any fixed constraints around caching/payload reuse (e.g., patient context never cached vs. non-PHI prompts ok to cache).

What we included in the draft: a token-sensitivity sim (token_sensitivity_sim.csv) with three scenarios (conservative / expected / optimistic), a recommended batching and prefetch strategy, and a pricing worksheet showing tokens/$ at our suggested reserved capacity tier. The MAP includes explicit acceptance criteria (latency < 400ms p95 for single-turn queries; unit cost target <$0.0008 per token for expected traffic using prefix caching).

Ben is looped for commercial/Q clarity. If you can confirm the three items above, we’ll run a tailored sim and lock the MAP schedule — target: pilot start in 4 weeks.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm token averages & caching constraints by EOD Thu 3/11.
2) We run a focused throughput sim and share results 3/12.
3) Finalize MAP & SOW by 3/16.

Attachments: MAP_Novena_v0.3.pdf (PDF), token_sensitivity_sim.csv (CSV), redwood_pricing_table_Q1_2027.xlsx (XLSX)

Chloe —

Appreciate the clear plan and the attachments. Quick answers up front:
- Peak CCU: our current expectation is 60 CCU for triage during peak hours, but we could see spikes to ~90 during rare events.
- Tokens: conservative (clinical triage): prompt 120 / response 450 average; scheduling flows: prompt 40 / response 60.
- Caching: patient-identifiable data will never be cached. Non-PHI system prompts (templates, routing prompts) can be cached; we want caching limited to non-PHI keys only.

Questions:
1) In your draft you list a prefix caching savings of ~35% — is that sensitive to the 450-token response assumption?
2) For batching, does Redwood batch across sessions or only within a single session? We need p95 latency guarantees for live triage.

Finance wants to see the tokens/$ sensitivity run with our numbers before we sign off on the MAP timeline. Can you run the sim using the triage 120/450 number and the 60–90 CCU range and return a short one-pager for Finance?

—Arman

Hi Arman —

Quick responses to your two questions, and I attached a short export of the sim I ran against your numbers (token_sensitivity_sim.csv).

1) Prefix caching sensitivity: the ~35% savings quoted is when 40–50% of prompts are template-driven (non-PHI) and the average response length is ~300 tokens. With a 450-token average response, savings drop to ~22–28% because response-side tokens dominate cost. In the attached CSV I included a row that uses 120/450 and shows ~24% cost reduction at 60 CCU with a 30s prefix cache TTL on non-PHI keys.

2) Batching behavior: Redwood supports cross-session batching at the serving runtime for compatible requests (stateless templates, short responses) and session-local batching for stateful KV-cache paths. For your live triage use-case (where p95 latency is critical), we recommend:
   - No cross-session batching on triage single-turn queries (to protect p95) unless they are explicitly marked as low-priority.
   - Use micro-batching (20–50ms packing window) for non-critical background queries (summaries, analytics) to preserve throughput economics.

Latency trade-offs: micro-batching adds ~12–20ms on average; cross-session batching can add 40–80ms depending on queue wait time. With the triage latency SLO of 400ms p95, we can safely enable a 20ms micro-batch window for any non-PHI template calls and rely on dedicated capacity with reserved pools to avoid queuing variance.

I recommend we run two simulations:
- Simulation A: strict p95 protection (no cross-session batching, micro-batch 20ms only on non-PHI).
- Simulation B: cost-optimized (aggressive prefix caching, 50ms micro-batches for non-critical calls).

I’ll run both and share a one-pager for Finance by EOD 3/12.

Attachments referenced: token_sensitivity_sim.csv (CSV) — includes scenario rows for 60 and 90 CCU with 120/450 tokens.

Thanks,
Karthik

Arman / Priya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the token numbers — that was exactly what we needed. Per Karthik’s note we ran Sim A/B with your 120/450 triage assumption and the 60/90 CCU range. Short one-pager is attached and I also uploaded the CSV and MAP to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNovenaMAP

Key takeaways (brief):
- With strict p95 protection (Sim A) and no cross-session batching for triage, expected unit cost at 60 CCU is $0.00095/token; at 90 CCU it rises to ~$0.00105/token because of more frequent model warmups.
- With cost-optimized settings (Sim B) and 30% template reuse, unit cost at 60 CCU drops to ~$0.00072/token, but p95 latency for triage can increase by ~30–60ms under burst.
- Prefix caching is most effective when non-PHI templates are >35% of prompts. Given your note that non-PHI templates exist but triage is mostly clinical text, realistic savings are in the 20–28% range for your profile.

Next steps: please confirm (a) acceptance of the MAP acceptance criteria as written, and (b) whether Novena requires the pilot to run with strict p95 protection (Sim A) or prefers a cost-optimized run (Sim B) where we’ll instrument stricter circuit breakers. Once you confirm we can finalize the SOW and kickoff 3/16.

Attachments: SimA_SimB_onepager.pdf (PDF), token_sensitivity_sim.csv (CSV), MAP_Novena_v0.3.pdf (PDF)

Best —
Chloe
